title: SYSK's 12 Days of Christmas… Toys: Hula-Hoops: The Toy That's A Shape
summary: Stuff You Should Know rerun-style playlist episode (introduced by Josh as a classic episode from the "12 Days of Christmas... Toys" playlist) on hula hoops. The hosts trace the hoop's history from ancient Egyptian and Greek children's play, ancient Briton "kill the hoop" games, the 14th-century British hula hoop craze, Native American hoop dancing (Tony White Cloud, 1930, national hoop dance competitions by 1991), and the Chunkey game at Cahokia. They explain the origin of the name "hula" from Polynesian dance noted by British sailors, Swiss Eurythmics training, and the Australian origin that inspired Wham-O's 1958 polyethylene hula hoop craze, including its trademark, sales, and later record attempts. They cover the physics (angular momentum, torque, centripetal force, friction, hip/knee/ankle motion), hoop exercise studies and calorie burn, hoop variants (ankle skipping, hoop rolling, hoop jumping, LED hoops, barbed-wire hoop performance), bans in Japan and Soviet criticism. The episode ends with a listener mail from Emily about recovering from anorexia and listening to the show with her sister Meghan.

segments.title: Playlist intro
segments.summary: Josh introduces the hula hoop episode as a classic from the playlist and sets up the topic.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts chat about hula hooping, a hoop dancer at an Atlanta festival, and the hosts' inability to hula hoop.

segments.title: Ancient and Native American hoop history
segments.summary: Hoops in ancient Egypt, Greece (Ganymede urn and possible Olympic link), ancient Britain's Kill the Hoop game and a 14th-century British hoop craze with injuries, the Cahokia Chunkey game, and Native American hoop dancing revived by Tony White Cloud in 1930 and national competitions by 1991.

segments.title: Polynesian origin of the word hula
segments.summary: British sailors in the 18th century noticed Polynesian hula dancing and applied the word hula to the hip-rotating hoop motion.

segments.title: Swiss Eurythmics and Australian roots
segments.summary: Emil Jaques-Dalcroze's Eurythmics program used hoops for fitness and dance; it spread to Britain and Australian PE classes, which the hosts link to Wham-O's modern hoop design.

segments.title: Wham-O and the 1958 craze
segments.summary: Richard Knerr and Arthur Melin made polyethylene hoops forty inches across for $1.98; about 100 million sold globally in 1958 before the fad faded; Wham-O trademarked the name hula hoop and the hoop was named a top toy by Time.

segments.title: Hoop contests and world records
segments.summary: National hula hoop contests ran 1968 to 1981; hula hoop songs were recorded; record attempts include Aaron Hibbs' 74-hour run in 2009 and Paul Blair's 132 hoops at once.

segments.title: Host anecdotes and a Coen Brothers tangent
segments.summary: Chuck recalls a costumed Surface Area Man in Athens and the hosts briefly discuss The Hudsucker Proxy, a fictional hula hoop invention story, before a break.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break with brief casual talk about Coen Brothers films.

segments.title: Hula hoop physics
segments.summary: Angular momentum, torque from hip rotation, centripetal force, gravity, and friction keep the hoop up; the key is moving the hips just ahead of the hoop's wave.

segments.title: Hips, knees and ankles in hooping
segments.summary: Studies from 2004 and a later one in the Journal of Human Movement Science found hips, knees and ankles drive hooping, with individuals using them in different proportions.

segments.title: Hoop variants and games
segments.summary: Hoop dancing, speed and endurance hooping, hoop rolling, ankle skipping (Belgian), hoop jumping, hoop returning, and hooping as a game of lava islands.

segments.title: Hoop fitness and modern hooping
segments.summary: Marisa Tomei took hoop fitness classes for The Wrestler; Michelle Obama hooped on the White House lawn; a study found about 210 calories burned in a half hour; LED hoops and burlesque hooping.

segments.title: Barbed Hula and hula hoop bans
segments.summary: Israeli artist Galit Landau's 2003 barbed wire hoop performance; the hoop was banned in Japan and criticized by the Soviets during the 1950s craze.

segments.title: Listener mail from Emily
segments.summary: Emily, turning eighteen, says the show helped her through anorexia recovery and brought her closer to her sister Meghan; the hosts respond and invite them to a Minneapolis show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give contact info and sign off, pointing listeners to HowStuffWorks.
